summary:
What if the way you eat is quietly deciding how fast you age?
David Sinclair is a Professor of Genetics at Harvard Medical School, one of the world's leading researchers on ageing and longevity, and the author of the New York Times bestseller Lifespan: Why We Age and Why We Don't Have To.
In this moment, David gives Steven a first-hand taste of what old age really feels like, and challenges what most of us assume about how long we'd actually want to live. He reveals the tiny "bodyguards" inside your cells that decide how quickly you age, the fasting window he aims for, the popular diet he's sceptical of, and the simple morning swap he made for his longevity.

title: Episode 677: Don't take her out (the principle of anti-dating)
summary:
Don’t take her out if you’re looking for a long-term relationship. Instead, court her in the context of the life you already lead. In this episode, I introduce the principle of anti-dating, arguing that conventional dates either provide irrelevant information or create a misleading idea of what an eventual relationship will look like. Inviting a potential partner into your everyday routine will reveal far more useful data than expensive dinners, elaborate activities, or structured interviews ever could.
